clue.text: Non-poetic writing about border plant

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the writing wraps around the border word

parts.note: writing that is not verse is prose
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A gardener writes plain notes on a plant growing in the border.
explanation.definitionFit: The primrose is a pale yellow spring-flowering wild plant.

clue.text: Country's head replaced by president in spring

indicators.note: the country's first letter is swapped out for the letter standing for president

parts.note: France is a country

explanation.surface: A nation's leader is ousted by its president one spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but is the verb: to leap or bound.
explanation.definitionFit: To prance is to bound or leap about lightly, as a lively horse does.

clue.text: From this, Mac's no exit, if working!

definitions.text: From this, Mac's no exit, if working!

indicators.note: working means the letters are put to work in a new arrangement

parts.note: the possessive 's adds no letter: just MAC
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Scot named Mac grumbles that, while he is employed, there is no escaping this levy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' signals the anagram of MAC, NO and EXIT, and the whole clue describes the tax: nobody in work can escape it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tax on earnings is deducted from everyone in employment, so a worker has no way out of it.

clue.text: River and mountain system in Russia, in the country

parts.note: the Urals are the mountain range dividing European and Asian Russia

explanation.surface: A traveller describes a river and mountains in Russia, out in the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural describes the countryside, away from towns, so it means belonging to the country.

clue.text: A meeting with no score that's vulnerable to attack

parts.note: a sitting is a session or meeting of a body such as a court or parliament
in cricket a duck is a batter's score of zero

explanation.surface: A goalless match leaves one side looking exposed to attack.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batter out without scoring has made a 'duck'.
explanation.definitionFit: An easy target that cannot defend itself, like a bird sitting still on water before a gun.

clue.text: Egyptian symbol to mark a book

parts.note: to scar is to leave a mark on

explanation.surface: Someone defaces a book with an ancient Egyptian emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: The dung beetle was sacred in ancient Egypt and its image was carved as an amulet.

clue.text: Happy about one name for a land mass

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the happy word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: content means satisfied or happy
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased about one name chosen for a newly found land.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the world's great divisions of land, such as Africa or Asia, is one of these.

clue.text: Some kangaroos try to do what birds do

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few kangaroos attempt to settle in the trees like birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds perch or settle for the night on a branch or ledge.

clue.text: The food to spoil in display

parts.note: bran is the husk of grain, eaten as food
to dish someone's chances is to ruin or spoil them

explanation.surface: Someone ruins the food that is laid out on show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'display' is a verb here: to wave something about for show.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish a sword or a document is to wave it about showily.

clue.text: Churchman to follow the account? Correct

indicators.note: to follow puts the churchman after the account

parts.note: a curate is an assistant to a parish priest

explanation.surface: A clergyman checks the accounts and asks whether they are correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means precise and free of error.

clue.text: A bit of grey in the girl's material

indicators.note: in puts the small piece inside the girl's name

parts.note: Nora is a girl's name

indicators.note: a bit of the word means just its first letter

explanation.surface: A thread of grey is caught in a girl's fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft yarn or cloth woven from the hair of a long-haired goat or rabbit.

clue.text: It holds items of inter est for a later age

definitions.text: It holds items of inter est for a later age

parts.words: It holds items of inter est for a later age
parts.note: a container buried or sealed with objects of the present day so future people can see how we lived

explanation.surface: A box packed with curiosities is kept for future generations.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealed container of contemporary objects stored for discovery in years to come.

clue.text: Fawn colour in lisle mackintosh making comeback

indicators.note: making comeback says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A raincoat of fine cotton in a pale brown shade returns to fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Lisle is a fine cotton thread; a mackintosh is a raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: The light yellowish-brown shade of a desert animal's coat, used as a colour name.

clue.text: Introduced it in a diet possibly

indicators.note: possibly says these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A dieter wonders whether something was slipped into the eating plan.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate is to start or bring in, as a new scheme or member.

clue.text: RN togs, worn but durable

indicators.note: worn suggests clothes battered out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Royal Navy clothing is threadbare yet still hard-wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: RN is the Royal Navy; togs are clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tough and hard-wearing lasts a long time.

clue.text: Work constrained, subdued

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
pressed means forced or constrained

explanation.surface: Under pressure at work, someone feels crushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Kept down or crushed by authority or harsh treatment.

clue.text: English unites issues

parts.note: merges means joins or unites

explanation.surface: England combines several matters into one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issues' is a verb here: comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Comes out or appears, as smoke issues from a chimney.

clue.text: Instruction for Luigi — need for translation?

indicators.note: translation turns words into another form, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: An Italian named Luigi asks whether he needs instructions translated.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle or rule giving direction on how to act.

clue.text: Clump of trees around the south growing closely together

indicators.note: around means the clump of trees surrounds the compass point

parts.note: a thicket is a dense group of bushes or trees
S is the abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: A dense copse stands to the south with trees packed tightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants set close and dense, or a stocky, heavily built figure.

clue.text: I have half-a dozen supporters

parts.note: supporters read as legs: a creature that stands on six of them, as an insect does

explanation.surface: A team boasts of having six loyal fans.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal with six legs, a term used of insects.

clue.text: See 4
"The wind in the willows" could displace this animal family

definitions.text: "The wind in the willows" could displace this

explanation.surface: A children's book about riverbank creatures seems to threaten a household of animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Willows bear fluffy flower spikes that the wind shakes loose; read as two words, the answer is a cat's relations.
explanation.definitionFit: Willows carry dangling flower spikes that wind scatters, and split in two the word gives a feline's relatives.

clue.text: See 11 down
Culmination of river in mature countryside finally

indicators.note: in puts the river inside the word for mature

parts.note: to age is to mature
the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: finally takes just the end letter of countryside

explanation.surface: A river reaches its highest point in the ripe countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest or farthest point, originally of an orbit, hence a climax.

clue.text: Small vessel following last course?

parts.note: vessel read as a drinking container, not a boat, used after the dessert at the end of a meal

explanation.surface: A small boat sets off on its final voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cup holding the after-dinner drink served once the meal is over.

clue.text: Faculty fellow's den

parts.note: F is an abbreviation for fellow
a lair is a wild animal's den

explanation.surface: A university fellow keeps a private study in the faculty.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural aptitude or talent, as a faculty for something.

clue.text: British general's parking signal

parts.note: Robert E Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War
P is the sign for parking

explanation.surface: A British officer's car park gives a warning signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A short high-pitched electronic tone used as a signal or alert.

clue.text: Large set of books for the fanatic

parts.note: big means large
OT is the Old Testament, a set of biblical books

explanation.surface: A huge library is meant for an obsessive reader.
explanation.definitionFit: An intolerant person blindly devoted to an opinion.

clue.text: Skimpy standard on board facing east

indicators.note: facing puts the compass point beside the rest
on board means aboard ship, inside the steamship letters

parts.note: board points to a ship, SS being a steamship
par is the standard or normal level

explanation.surface: The regulation kit aboard an eastbound ship is meagre.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'on board' is being inside SS, the usual crossword ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinly scattered or scanty, not plentiful.

clue.text: Friendly, but leaving

explanation.surface: A sociable person is on the way out.
explanation.definitionFit: Sociable and extrovert; also departing, as a retiring office-holder.

clue.text: Angry speech from one in commerce

indicators.note: in puts the numeral inside the word for commerce

parts.note: trade means commerce
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A businessman launches into a furious rant.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, angry denunciation or harangue.

clue.text: Playfully tease the art lover

indicators.note: playfully suggests letters frolicking into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone mischievously ribs a connoisseur of art.
explanation.definitionFit: A person with refined appreciation of beauty and the arts.
